blocks.text:
I need to work out which chain A residues (3-152) lie close enough to chain B residues (341-361) to form contacts, so I'm mapping out the coordinate ranges each chain occupies and scanning chain A atoms that fall near chain B's spatial region.

I'm checking residue K341 specifically against nearby chain A residues, noting that chain A residues around positions 3-13 and 28-31 have z-values overlapping with B341's z range near 12-19, so those are candidates worth checking atom-by-atom for actual contact distances.

I'm scanning chain A for atoms with positive x and high z values near chain B's K341, checking residues like SER29, GLU30, ARG7, LYS14, LYS75, and PHE77, but none seem to have coordinates close enough to be neighbors — suggesting K341 may lack a chain A contact partner.

Then I catch A:SER152 at (9.0, -5.4, 12.19), which is actually a match, along with nearby ASP151, ASN150, and TRP149.

Now checking chain B residues with negative y values — ARG343, LYS344, HIS346, LYS347, and others — to see if their coordinates line up similarly with a positive x and z region.

This suggests the peptide's C-terminal segment (residues 348-361) sits near chain A's C-terminal region, so I want to map the interface systematically by comparing coordinate clusters between chain A residues 145-152 and chain B residues 341-361.

Still mapping residue coordinates...

Continuing to trace residue coordinates through this chain segment, then shifting focus to identify chain A atoms within the surrounding spatial region.

Checking that too—still too far given the y-coordinate gap between the chains. Residue 7 ARG is also far based on its x-range, so I'm continuing to scan chain A atoms with z >= 5, checking each against chain B's coordinate ranges to narrow down which residues could actually be in contact.

Checking A residues 15-26, most sit too low in z. I find a promising contact though: A:SER25's OG atom sits close to B:ALA357's CB, only about 3.8 apart, which looks like a real interaction worth tracking.

Given this, I need to be systematic about scanning both chains. I'm defining a bounding box for chain A atoms likely near the interface, then plan to walk through each chain A residue in order, comparing coordinates against chain B to identify all contacts.

Continuing through residues 10-14, checking distances against nearby chain B atoms — most are too far apart to count as contacts, so I keep moving down the sequence.

Now I'm checking LEU16 and GLN17 side chain atoms against B:LEU353, again finding distances too large to register as contacts, so both residues get skipped.

Moving on to GLU18 and ASP19, whose x-coordinates fall outside the relevant range near chain B partners like LYS359, so I'm skipping these too and turning attention to PRO20's coordinate range instead.

Checking PRO21's atoms against nearby B chain residues like TYR361 and ALA357 — the distances are too large, so no contacts there either. Now moving to VAL22's coordinates.

Continuing to check GLY23's atoms against nearby B-chain residues like TYR361, ARG358, and ALA357, computing distances to see if any fall within contact range.

This manual pairwise approach is too slow with 1205 x 185 atoms. I should instead narrow down by comparing chain B CA coordinates against chain A CAs within a rough 10 Å window to identify likely interface residues before checking finer atom distances.

Now I'm cataloging chain A's CA coordinates, continuing through residues 3 through 13 to map out their spatial positions.

Still listing coordinates...

Still computing atom coordinates...

Now I have all the A chain CA positions I need, so I'm shifting to comparing them against the B chain CAs to find residues within about 12 Å of each other, starting with B341 against A152.

Checking the distance between B341's N atom and A152's C atom gives about 7.2 Å, too far for a contact, so that pairing doesn't work.

Checking A73 LEU's side chain atoms against B341 also shows large separations, no contact there either. Chain A doesn't seem to have atoms reaching into the x~12, z~13 region except possibly around A150, so B341 likely has no contacts at all.

Turning to B342 TYR, I'm laying out its full set of atom coordinates to compare against nearby chain A residues.

Checking distances from CA to A152, A29, A56, A73, and A30, none of these fall within a close contact range, so I'm now looking at the tyrosine's OH group to see if it interacts with any nearby serine.

I compute the distance between B:Y342's OH and A:SER29's OG and find they're only about 3.35 Å apart -- that's a genuine contact. So chain B TYR342 makes contact with A:SER29. I need to keep going systematically through the remaining residues.

The interface spans chain A regions around 24-29, 35-42, 53-57, 69-75, and 145-152. I'm checking each candidate A residue's CA against chain B CAs to find close pairs -- A24 VAL comes out around 4.6 Å from B357, making it a likely interface residue, and I'm continuing this check into A25 SER.

A25 SER pairs at roughly 5.3 Å from B357 and 5.7 Å from B353, also qualifying. A26 GLY sits about 6.6 Å from B353, still a candidate, while A27 ALA and A28 PRO are farther out at 7.8-9.4 Å, borderline but possibly still relevant to the interface.

A29 SER is close to B349 at 7.6 Å, confirming a contact already noted with B342's hydroxyl, and A30 GLU comes in around 8.3 Å from B349. A31 ASN and the A32-34 stretch drift further away, into the 10-12 Å range, making them weak or unlikely contacts.

For A35 GLN, the backbone CA is quite distant from B353 and B349, but I'm checking the side chain atoms since they extend outward — comparing the CD2 of B342 against A35's NE2 to see if the glutamine's tail reaches closer than the backbone suggests.

Moving to A36 TRP, the CA distances to B353 and B349 are still fairly large, so I'm now checking the tryptophan's bulky indole ring side chain atoms to see if any of those extend into contact range.

Nothing in the negative-y region seems close enough, so I'm shifting to think more broadly about chain B's overall shape—likely an amphipathic helix—to figure out which A residues could face its negative-y side.

I'll try scanning chain A atoms directly for a bounding box covering the likely interface region (roughly x -14 to 16, y -16 to 8, z -3 to 21), then walking through chain A residues sequentially to see which fall into it—starting near residues 3-12, checking their CA coordinates against those bounds.

Looking at residue 12's atoms against the closest chain B atoms, the distances are quite large (dx around 7-9 units and more), so this residue is too far from the B chain to be part of the interface.

Now checking residue 13 (PHE), I compare its coordinates against nearby B chain atoms like B352 and B353, but find these too are around 8+ units away. However, B356's side chain atoms (CG, CD, NE2, OE1) sit at x -8 to -10, y -7 to -9, which puts them in range of chain A atoms with similar coordinates, so I need to check which A residues fall near x -9 to -13, y -7 to -9, z 7-10.

Scanning candidates, GLN17's CD is close in x but its y is off at -2.5, and PRO20's backbone is too shallow in z. Looking at PRO20's CB and CG side chain atoms, the y values line up around -7, but z sits too low at 5.3-6.0 compared to B356's NE2 near z 7.5, so this pairing still seems too far to count as contact.

I'm listing out A20's proline atom coordinates and computing distances from B356's NE2 to each: CB comes out closest at 4.04, still slightly above the 4.0 cutoff, so I'm checking CA and other nearby atoms too.

Since A20/A21 don't pan out, I'm scanning for other A chain residues closer to B356 spatially. I'm comparing B356's CA position against nearby A chain CA coordinates, checking A22 and starting to look at A23's distance.

Comparing A25's CB position against B356's CB, I calculate a distance of about 3.92 Å, which is well within contact range. This confirms B:Q356 contacts A:S25.

Confirmed, that's another contact. Given how many borderline cases there are near 4 Å, I need a systematic approach: for each chain B residue, find all chain A atoms within a reasonable radius and compute distances, using a coarse spatial grouping of chain A residues by region to make this tractable.

I'm identifying the likely interface residues on chain A by checking which CA atoms fall within about 14 Å of any chain B CA, then verifying those candidates with actual pairwise distance calculations.

Continuing through residues A40 to A42, checking CA distances against nearby B-chain candidates like B357, B354, and B358 to find contacts under roughly 7 Å.

Checking B361's tyrosine ring atoms against A42's backbone — the hydroxyl oxygen OH comes out to about 2.60 Å from A42's carbonyl O, which is a real contact. So B:TYR361 does interact with A:GLY42's O atom.

Moving to A43 proline, I check its CA and N against B361 OH but those distances land around 4.6-4.7 Å, too far to count as contacts.

Since I only need chain B residues, my real task is scanning each B residue for any chain A atom within 4 Å. I'm now working through B341 lysine, checking its position against nearby chain A atoms like A150 asparagine's coordinates.

I check the y-coordinates and find A150's atoms sit well below B341's range, with a minimum distance gap over 5.8 Å, ruling out contact. I also verify A152 serine's atoms against B341's nitrogen, computing a distance around 7.2 Å, confirming no contact there either, and now I'm considering chain A residues 73-75 next.

I check the z-coordinates for lysine 75 and leucine 73 side chains against B341's NZ atom, finding gaps too large for contact, so B341 appears to have no binding partner - likely it's an exposed N-terminal residue. B342 tyrosine is confirmed with a real contact between its OH and A:SER29's OG at 3.35 Å. Now I'm pulling the atomic coordinates for B343 arginine's backbone and side chain to check for contacts.

I'm scanning chain A residues near arginine 343's side chain, looking at Leu73 and Ser74 coordinates, and finding CD is roughly 3-4 Å from CD1 of Leu73 — close enough to flag as a potential contact.

Now I'm checking other nearby candidates like Ser152, but the distances are too far, so I'm moving to check Lys54's position instead.

I'm also checking A:ASP151's oxygen against B343's NE and CZ atoms, both landing around 4.25-4.34 apart, and continuing to compare against the NH atom too.

Still no strong match nearby, so I'm scanning other residues like GLN147, SER148, PHE72's ring, and VAL70 to see if any of their atoms fall within range of the target instead.

All the distances I'm finding hover right around 4.0-4.2, none clearly under the cutoff, so I want to recompute the closest candidate (A73's CD1) more carefully to make sure I'm not missing the true contact due to rounding error.

Checking a few more candidate pairs near B343's guanidinium group against A151's backbone oxygen, but all distances come out above 4 Å. It seems B343's closest contact is right around 4.02 Å, just at the threshold.

I should double-check by scanning through chain A more carefully for atoms in the relevant coordinate range I might have overlooked, going through residues like A46 and A52 to see if their side chains fall closer.

Continuing to log coordinates for residues A55 and A56, tracking backbone and side-chain atom positions...

Continuing through the coordinate data for residues 72 through 75, tracking PHE, LEU, SER, and LYS positions as I move toward the lower z-values near residue 147.

Now recording residues 147 through 149 - GLN, SER, and TRP - with their backbone and side chain atom coordinates as I build out this structural map.

Continuing to log residue coordinates through A152, then checking distances for B343 contacts—A73 CD1 comes out around 4.02-4.94 Å depending on the atom pair, and I'm now computing B343 CA against A152 N to see if it falls within contact range.

Confirmed: distance 3.78Å, within contact range. Now moving to B344 LYS, listing its atom coordinates and checking proximity to nearby A152 residue atoms.

Checking B344's backbone atoms against A152 — the distances I'm getting are mostly in the 4.5-5Å range, which is right at the edge and likely outside contact threshold. Since A152 is the C-terminal residue and B344 sits above it, I'm leaning toward no real contact here, but I want to double-check other nearby possibilities before ruling it out.

Moving to B345, a lysine residue — I'm laying out its atom coordinates and starting to scan chain A atoms with higher z-values to look for the nearest neighbors.

All chain A candidates near it have negative x while B345's x values sit around 6-8, so the distance is too large — no contact there. Moving on to B346, a histidine, I'm listing its atom positions and now checking chain A residues with x roughly 0-6, y between -2 and 4, and z near 13 for potential proximity.

I check B346 CD2 against A29 OG and find they're close enough (~3.20 Å) to count as a contact, so H346 on chain B is in contact. Now I'm moving on to check B347 LYS's atoms for potential contacts too.

Looking through chain A for atoms with higher z-values that might be near B347's position, I check A152's OG and CB but they're too far from B347's O and C atoms. I continue scanning chain A residues like A3, A6, and A10 with z≥13 to see if any fall within contact range.

No matches emerge in that region, so B347 appears to have no contact with chain A. I move on to check B348 SER's coordinates against nearby chain A residues.

Checking B349's coordinates against nearby chain A residues, I'm looking at A29 SER and computing whether its OG or backbone atoms fall within contact distance based on the y and z offsets.

I confirm A29 SER OG sits about 3.49Å from B349's OE1, close enough to count as a contact. Now scanning B350 PHE's coordinates to see if any of its atoms also fall within range of chain A.

Checking distances between B350's ring atoms and A37's OD1/CG positions, none of them come close enough to indicate a real contact—all around 4 Å or more.

Now moving to check B351 GLN's atom coordinates against nearby residues for potential contacts.

Scanning further through chain A residues for any atoms with negative y and z above 9, I'm not finding a match, so it looks like B351 likely has no contact with chain A in that region.

Now I'm checking B352 LEU's coordinates against chain A to determine if there's a contact there.

I don't see chain A atoms matching the coordinates near B352, so that's likely no contact. Now checking B353 LEU's coordinates against nearby chain A residues to look for potential contacts.

Confirming that distance also falls under 4Å, so B:VAL353 counts as a contact. Now I'm checking B354 VAL's backbone and sidechain coordinates against nearby chain A residues within the relevant coordinate range.

Checking the CG2 distance gives about 4.6, too far for contact. I'm scanning chain A for any atom in that x/y/z window near B354, but it looks like this pocket is actually empty on chain A's side, meaning chain B occupies a groove there without a close A neighbor. Let me verify by checking A53's CB too, which also comes up too far, so B354 may simply lack a qualifying contact.

Now moving to B355 ASP, I'm listing out its backbone and sidechain coordinates to start checking distances to chain A residues.

For B355, I look at nearby chain A residues but find nothing within range, so no contact there. B356 GLN, though, does contact A:S25 CB at 3.92, so that's a hit.

Moving to B357 ALA, I extract its backbone and CB coordinates, then compare CB against A:SER25's OG position, getting a small delta of about 0.6 in the x-direction, suggesting a close contact worth checking further.

Continuing through B358's ARG side chain coordinates out to the guanidinium group, then scanning nearby chain A residues in that x,y,z region for potential contacts, starting with A41 PHE.

Confirmed: distance ~3.50, B:ARG358 is in contact. Now checking B359 LYS coordinates against nearby chain A atoms in the same spatial region to look for additional contacts.

Checking B360's coordinates against chain A residues, but nothing in that y-range lines up closely enough for a contact.

I'm continuing to check residues around A45-A47 and A129-135 for spatial proximity, finding no contacts there, but confirming B361 TYR does contact A:GLY42's oxygen at 2.61 Å. Now I need to go back and re-verify B341-B345, B348, and several other residues I'd initially marked as having no contact, starting with B354.

For B352 LEU, I'm listing out its atomic coordinates and cross-referencing against all chain A atoms with z ≥ 9, scanning through residues 3, 4, 6, and 7 to check their positions systematically.

Continuing to log coordinate ranges for residues 14, 17, 27, and 28, tracking atom positions to narrow down their spatial locations in the structure.

Continuing through res32 asparagine coordinates, then moving into res33 isoleucine and res34 methionine backbone and side chain atom positions.

Now I'm cataloging residues 35 through 37 - glutamine, tryptophan, and asparagine - checking their atom coordinates against the relevant y-range criteria, then scanning residues 150-152 for matching backbone atoms in the target z-range.

Compiling the final list of chain A residues with z>9: residues 3, 6, 7, 10, 13, 14, 17, 27-37, and 150-152. Now moving on to check chain B, starting around residue 352.

I checked B352's coordinates against everything in the z>9 list and none of the distances are close enough for contact — it's ruled out. For B351, I'm measuring distances to residue 152's atoms, finding some pairs around 5-6 Å apart but continuing to check closer pairs to confirm whether it's a real contact.

Now I'm scanning through chain A atoms with y < -6 and z > 5 to identify candidates near B354's region, starting with residues 20 and 54.

Checking the closest distances confirms B354 has no chain A contact. For B355, chain A's nearest residue is TRP149's ring atoms, which are still too far away (x differs by 7-9 units), so no contact there either. B359 also checks out as no contact.

Now I'm looking at B360, comparing its atoms against VAL22 in chain A -- the closest distance comes out to about 4 angstroms.

I keep trying other atom pairs between B360 and A22/A23, computing distances of 4.8-5.7, none coming close enough to the 4.0 threshold, so I'm still searching for a valid contact.

B361 already checked out fine at 2.61. Now I'm going back through B344, B341, B345, and B347/348 to double check my earlier "no contact" conclusions, starting with B344's atoms against A150-152, computing coordinate differences to find the true minimum distance.

Continuing to check distances between residue atoms, computing 4.79 for A152 CB and moving on to check A150 OD1 against nearby atoms.
